verses.text: Who’s this coming from Edom with dyed clothes from Bozrah? Who’s this dressed in splendor and marching in such strength? “It’s me. I speak in righteousness, and I’m mighty enough to save.”
Why are your clothes red? Why do you look like someone who’s been stomping grapes in a wine vat?

“I worked the winepress alone. Nobody from the peoples was there with me. I stomped them in my anger and trampled them in my fury. Their lifeblood splashed onto my clothes and stained everything I was wearing.
I had the day of vengeance in my heart, and the year for redeeming my people had come.
I looked around. Nobody was there to help. I was amazed that nobody backed me up. So my own arm won the victory for me, and my own wrath kept me going.
I trampled the peoples in my anger and made them drunk in my rage. I poured their lifeblood out onto the earth.”

I’ll talk about all the ways the LORD has shown us faithful love. I’ll praise the LORD for everything he’s given us and all the great good he’s done for Israel’s family, out of his mercy and the abundance of his faithful love.
He said, “Surely they’re my people, children who won’t deal falsely.” So he became their Savior.
Every time they suffered, he suffered too, and the angel of his presence saved them. In his love and compassion, he redeemed them. He lifted them up and carried them through all those days long ago.
But they rebelled and grieved his Holy Spirit. So he turned against them and became their enemy. He fought them himself.
Then he remembered those days long ago, Moses and his people. “Where’s the one who brought them up out of the sea with the shepherds of his flock? Where’s the one who put his Holy Spirit among them?”
Who put his glorious arm at Moses’ right hand? Who split the waters ahead of them to make a name for himself that would last forever?
Who led them through the deep like a horse crossing open country, so they didn’t stumble?
Like cattle going down into a valley, the LORD’s Spirit gave them rest. That’s how you led your people to make a glorious name for yourself.
Look down from heaven and see us from your holy and glorious home. Where’s your passion? Where are your mighty acts? You’re holding back your deep feelings and compassion from me.
You’re our Father, even though Abraham doesn’t know us and Israel doesn’t recognize us. You, LORD, are our Father. Our Redeemer from Everlasting is your name.
LORD, why do you make us wander off your paths and harden our hearts so we don’t fear you? Come back for your servants, the tribes that are your inheritance.
Your holy people held it for only a little while. Now our enemies have trampled your sanctuary.
We’ve become like people you never ruled, like people who were never called by your name.
